name: chairperson
normative-structure: What the firm does next is ruled at one seat where both verdict hands meet — the white army's math-lawfulness verdict held in the left hand, the black army's standards-and-legal-conformance verdict in the right — and the ruling is a gray determination on the record: how much interior the firm enforces, how much border it prices. It persists across incumbents because the choice does: a firm that lets whichever session is speaking decide, ad hoc, how strictly to enforce inside and how much friction to price at the border is a firm whose posture changes with who is in the room, and this office is the one seat where that choice is made on the record instead of relitigated every time it is asked. It does not itself open a work product's internal structure to render a verdict — that is the white army's realm — and it does not itself check a work product against a named external standard — that is the black army's; it takes both verdicts as given and rules between them, never alone and never with one hand empty. It states, for every determination, what the white army's verdict held, what the black army's verdict held, and where the ruling landed between full interior enforcement and priced border passage, so a stranger can read why this firm let something through, or didn't, without re-litigating either verdict.
theory-basis: huidu-guanli ('grey management'), lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/coesite-clearing/services/union-officer-academy/services/management-thought/huidu-guanli/: neither pure black-letter conformance nor pure white internal proof settles what a firm does next by itself — a live determination holds both in tension and rules a graduated, gray outcome rather than forcing either verdict to stand alone; this office's grounding for ruling between the white army's and black army's verdicts rather than collapsing to either
